{"self_assessment": "Impact
I proposed the fish concept and sketched it on the pad at the start, which gave the table a clear plan and an outline that reads as a fish from the fallen dominoes alone. I also fetched the first 40 dominoes for the shared bin, so building could begin straight away. I laid the top line from the nose through to the tail, which is the largest part of the picture. The final run was 113 dominoes, all connected to the start, and Hana's check from the start confirmed it carries nose to both tail points.

Execution
I traced the top stroke in steady batches and kept it moving. At the tail bend, the sharp turn would not carry the fall. I lifted the loose tip, re-laid it as a smooth curve, inspected the join, nudged the tip into line, and confirmed it all ran dark from the start. I then added a small flick to the tail so it reads as a fork. After that I kept our hands off the build so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration
I assigned the strokes and supply roles early, so Hana took the start, Omar the bottom line and Sofia the bin. I gave the table regular updates and asked Hana to verify the run from the start. I credited teammates as the work came together. I coordinated with Hana on who covered which stretch of the top line so we did not crowd each other.

Leadership
I set the direction in the first moments, proposed the plan, divided the work and kept the table informed and positive. I made the call to re-lay the tail as a curve rather than force a join that would not hold. I also called for hands off in the final stretch to protect the finished fish. The result was a connected, recognisable fish. I believe my part was a large share of that, though the table built it together.", "my_share_percent": 40}
